subject: project:gdl
value:
WHEN A PROOF RUNS AGAINST A PERMUTED STREAM IT MUST BE HANDED THE PERMUTED RELOCATION SET, OR IT PRODUCES FALSE REFUSALS THAT READ EXACTLY LIKE PROPERTIES OF THE FUNCTION. This extends claim.law.HV_permute-payload-check-does-not-bind-a-relocation-to-its-atom.20260901.v1 from the payload/binding question to the PROOF-INPUT question, which is a separate surface and was not covered.

THE KNOWN HALF. HV establishes that relocations ride their atom and that the deriving agent must bind them to their destination slots. CH's ch_closable.py already applies this to verify_consistent_recolor: it maps every in-window relocation through the permutation, keyed by the owning instruction, and records that passing the un-permuted offsets 'makes a Tier B verdict unsound'. Correct, and the same reasoning has a second consumer nobody had reached, because the combined stage's value obligation did not exist when that was written.

THE UNCOVERED HALF, MEASURED. prove_constant_dataflow takes `relocated_indexes` and resets its fact unconditionally at any word carrying a non-immediate-only relocation, and additionally refuses to let a relocated word BE the definition -- both correct and deliberately fail-closed, since an unresolved address half is not the literal the proof requires. Hand it the UN-permuted set alongside the PERMUTED words and the index set no longer describes the stream it is reading: whichever word LANDS on a formerly-relocated offset inherits a relocation that actually rode a different atom.

ON update_chinfo this is exactly fatal and exactly silent. Our raw stream has the SDA21-relocated `lwz r0,0(r0)` at +0x6c and `li r22,0` at +0x70; the permutation swaps them, so after it the DEFINITION `li r22,0` sits at +0x6c -- a formerly-relocated offset. With the un-permuted index set the prover marks that word relocated, refuses it as a definition, and reports `r22 is not provably 0 on every path reaching +0x84`. It reports the SAME sentence for all 31 GPRs, so the site presents as having no provable source at all and the function reads as refusing on the value obligation. With the remap applied, r22 PROVES, and it is the UNIQUE register that does; the function closes byte-exact. Nothing about the function changed between the two runs.

WHY THIS IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN MERELY WRONG. The failure is fail-CLOSED, so it can never produce an unsound rule -- it can only ever hide a real one. That is what makes it expensive: a fail-closed bug generates no alarm, produces a plausible refusal message naming the function and the register, and is indistinguishable by inspection from the genuine 'the value is not provable here' verdict that the same code path emits legitimately. It is a direct instance of AGENTS.md discipline 14 -- a guard's refusal measures the guard, not only the function -- and the tell that separates the two is cheap and worth naming: IF EVERY REGISTER REFUSES A CONSTANT THAT IS VISIBLY LOADED NEARBY, SUSPECT THE PROOF'S INPUTS BEFORE THE FUNCTION. A genuine unprovable site usually has a plausible cause on inspection (an interposed indirect call, a merge from a path that does not define the value); 31-for-31 refusals with a `li rN,K` sitting six instructions above the site is an instrument fault.

THE RULE FOR ANY FUTURE DERIVER. Every artefact derived from the object must be permuted together, as one step, whenever a permutation is applied: the words, the relocation offsets (keyed by the owning instruction, instruction-floored per the SDA21 offset law), and the jumptable offsets. Permuting the words alone is the natural mistake because the words are what the eye checks. A second, cheaper instance of the same family also cost a derivation here: reconstructing region relocation records with a fabricated addend of 0 instead of reading the real (offset,type,addend) triples out of the object's own RELA section makes _relocation_sha256 disagree with the hash apply_patch computes, and the rule dies as `instruction permutation relocation input hash changed` -- which reads as a permutation defect and is an authoring defect. Read the triples; never reconstruct them.
